chromiumOracle.line: Intl.v8BreakIterator({type: "line"}); Intl.Segmenter has no line granularity

platformIcu.linux-x64: system ICU (Ubuntu 24.04 runner); invariants checked, version reported by rv_text_segmentation_version in the CI log
platformIcu.linux-arm64: system ICU (Ubuntu 24.04 arm runner); invariants checked, version in the CI log
platformIcu.osx-arm64: system libicucore; invariants checked, version in the CI log

qualifications.name: full stop between letters
qualifications.reason: UAX #29 WB6/WB7 keep a full stop between letters inside one word (MidNumLet), as the engine's ICU does; Chromium breaks there.

qualifications.name: Hangul jamo join
qualifications.reason: ICU puts a word boundary inside the grapheme cluster of conjoining jamo and a syllable; the engine joins the two segments so no grapheme splits, where Chromium splits it.

qualifications.name: resolved locale
qualifications.reason: The engine reports ICU's valid locale; the Windows slim ICU data keeps only English locale resources, so most tags resolve to root. Chromium falls back to the browser default (en-GB here) for unknown tags.

qualifications.name: line oracle
qualifications.reason: No standard browser line segmenter exists; the oracle is Chromium's non-standard Intl.v8BreakIterator.

qualifications.name: system ICU
qualifications.reason: Linux and macOS segmentation follows the system ICU version; exact results are measured on ICU 77.1.
